chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn al-Hakam from Muthanna ibn al-Walid al-Hannat from Abi Basir who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: "When one of you marries, what does he do?" I said to him: "I do not know, may I be your ransom."

He said: "When he intends to do so, let him pray two rak'ahs and praise Allah and say: 'O Allah, I intend to marry, O Allah, decree for me from among the women who are most chaste in their private parts, and most protective of themselves for me and of my wealth, and most abundant in provision, and greatest in blessing. And decree for me from her a good offspring, whom You make a righteous successor in my life and after my death.'

When she is brought to him, let him place his hand on her forehead and say: 'O Allah, by Your Book I married her, and in Your trust I took her, and by Your words I made lawful her private part. If You have decreed in her womb an offspring, make him a Muslim, sound and whole, and do not make him the share of Satan.'

I said: "And how can it be the share of Satan?" He said: "Indeed, when the man approaches the woman and sits in his place, Satan is present with him. If he remembers the name of Allah, Satan withdraws from him. And if he acts and does not mention the name, Satan enters his member, so the action is from both of them together and the seed is one."
I said: "By what is this known, may I be your ransom?" He said: "By our love and our hatred."

key_terms.أَعَفَّهُنَّ فَرْجاً: Most chaste in their private parts
key_terms.بِحُبِّنَا وَ بُغْضِنَا: By our love and our hatred (referring to the Imams)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended supplication and ritual for a Muslim man when marrying and consummating the marriage?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* details the specific supplications and ritual actions for marriage, emphasizing the selection of a chaste and blessed wife through prayer and invocation. It further explains the spiritual dynamics of consummation, noting that Satan's presence is repelled by remembering Allah's name, and links the spiritual quality of the offspring to the love and hatred of the Ahl al-Bayt.
